title: Microsoft Purview: protect data sent to unmanaged cloud apps through the Island Enterprise Browser
summary: Hold: the DLP automation creates a policy container rather than configuring its audit or block rules. The PowerShell reference also explicitly documents the Network enforcement plane, contrary to the table note. The rollout, administrator-controlled default and mixed licensing are supported.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans an Island integration with Purview network data security.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview network data security now integrates with Island, extending protection to Island’s browser-based workflows at the point of user interaction.

claims.claim: New and existing Island customers can configure collection and DLP policies for unmanaged cloud app data shared through the Island Enterprise Browser, Island Extension and browser add-ins.
claims.quote: new and existing Island customers can configure Microsoft Purview collection and data loss prevention policies to detect and protect data shared with unmanaged cloud apps through the Island Enterprise Browser, the Island Extension, and browser add ins

claims.claim: The roadmap describes HTTP and HTTPS coverage.
claims.quote: browser add ins via HTTP and HTTPS

claims.claim: The integration uses the same classifiers, sensitive information types and sensitivity labels as other Purview policies.
claims.quote: using the same classifiers, sensitive information types, and sensitivity labels used in other Purview policies.

claims.claim: Island provides presentation-layer visibility and control over typed and pasted input, file transfers and extension activity before data leaves the browser.
claims.quote: Island provides visibility and control at the presentation layer, including typed and pasted input, file transfers, and extension activity, so data can be inspected before it ever leaves the browser.

claims.claim: The integration enriches Data Security Posture Management.
claims.quote: This integration further enriches Purview Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)

claims.claim: The integration enriches the Insider Risk Management risk score.
claims.quote: Insider Risk Management (IRM) risk score

claims.claim: The integration supports data security and compliance for AI interactions.
claims.quote: enables data security and compliance for AI interactions

claims.claim: The DLP UI route runs through Data loss prevention, Policies, Create policy, Inline web traffic, Custom and Custom policy to the Network and non-Microsoft secure browsers enforcement option.
claims.quote: Select + Add cloud apps. Select the Adaptive app scopes tab, then choose All unmanaged AI apps and select Add (1). Select Edit scope on All unmanaged AI apps.
claims.fix: Replace the path with 'Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Inline web traffic > Custom > Custom policy > + Add cloud apps > Adaptive app scopes > All unmanaged AI apps > Edit scope > Include only specific > + Add inclusions > Specific users and groups > group > Choose where to enforce the policy > Network and non-Microsoft secure browsers'. State that this is the cited unmanaged-AI scenario, with the administrator choosing the target group. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-create-policy-ai-network-data-security.

claims.claim: New-DlpCompliancePolicy -Name <String> -EnforcementPlanes <MultiValuedProperty> is the automation for network DLP policies that audit or block data.
claims.quote: Use the New-DlpCompliancePolicy cmdlet to create data loss prevention (DLP) policies in the Microsoft Purview compliance portal. DLP policies contain DLP rules that identify, monitor, and protect sensitive information.
claims.fix: Narrow this existing row's governs to 'Network enforcement plane for a new DLP policy', and use 'New-DlpCompliancePolicy -Name <String> -EnforcementPlanes Network'. Retain the qualification that this creates only the policy container, not its Audit only/Block rules. The Network value is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/new-dlpcompliancepolicy.

claims.claim: The New-DlpCompliancePolicy reference lists no value for network policies.
claims.quote: The EnforcementPlanes parameter defines the layer where policy actions are run. ... Valid values are: ... Network
claims.fix: Replace 'The reference read lists no value for network policies' with 'The EnforcementPlanes parameter accepts Network', citing https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/new-dlpcompliancepolicy.

claims.claim: The collection-policy UI route uses the documented collection-policy, classifier, activity and unmanaged-cloud-app steps to reach Network and non-Microsoft secure browsers.

claims.fix: Shorten controls[2].ui.path to 'Data loss prevention > Classifiers > Collection policies', the documented page listing these policies, rather than printing an incomplete wizard route. Add to its note: 'This path opens the collection-policy list; the cited network scenario gives the subsequent activity, app scope, content capture and network-enablement choices.' Keep https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/collection-policies-create-deploy-policy as docs.
